text:
leah: thinking out loudwe've tried eager demote + compaction and saw good steady-state memory but bad p95 spikes during batch bursts. what if instead of full-blob migration we do a scatter-gather tiled copy that keeps large contiguous runs intact and only relocates hot tiles?
samir: tiled-copy sounds promising. helps reduce fragmentation by preserving untouched runs. concern: metadata explosion (per-tile residency bitsets).
ben: metadata ok if we compress it. e.g., run-length encode tile bitsets per allocation. overhead <1% for typical slabs. also we can keep tile size adaptive: 16MB for KV slabs, 256KB for activations.
ty: adaptive tile sizes + run-length encoding = cool, but PCIe and CPU memcpy behavior varies. bigger tiles prefer DMA throughput, small tiles favor parallelism. add heuristic to pick tile size based on bandwidth util.
ops-bot: perf-run: canary pool 'tile-evict-a' booted. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/tile-evict-a
leah: interface question: do we expose tile affinity in allocator API or keep it internal? exposing could let upper layers mark hot offsets (KV knows hot keys).
samir: expose minimal hint API: allocator.hint_hot(range) and allocator.hint_cold(range). leave strict semantics to runtime (best-effort). that keeps ABI stable.
ben: tradeoffs: exposing hints helps KV and cache layers but increases coupling. also need atomic pointer swaps when we relocate tiles out-of-band. otherwise indexes point to old phys.
ty: suggest atomic relocation protocol: 1) allocate destination, 2) memcpy tiled range, 3) CAS update index to new pointer, 4) free old tile. If CAS fails, retry or merge changes.
leah: that works for same-host moves. what about host->host streaming (staging to CPU then to other node)? latency sensitive though.
samir: for host->host we should do staged-copy with backpressure and a reservation token so we don't oversubscribe tenant vram during multi-hop. reservation token semantics: reserve N bytes on dest before copy.
ben: add per-tenant reservation accounting so peak_vram respects quotas. if reservation denied, fall back to mark-for-evict. metric: reservation_denials.
ty: fragmentation: tiled moves leave gaps. propose a "hole coalescer" background job that merges adjacents during low-util windows. coalescer needs to be tenant-aware and rate-limited.
leah: coalescer should prefer long-run merges to avoid oscillation. maybe only merge if combined free size > threshold and host bandwidth idle.
samir: also think about pinned stages: if we stream tile-by-tile and a writer mutates middle, need write-protect and a retry path. simplest: page-fault-and-retry loop with optimistic copy.
ben: code sketch: ```
// migrate tile
alloc(dest);
write_protect(src);
memcpy(dest, src, n);
if (writer_detected(src)) { undo or retry }
CAS(index, src, dest);
unprotect(dest);
free(src);
```
ty: encrypted pages: on Private, we cannot decrypt on staging host without KMS. streaming requires remote unwrap or destination with KMS access. if not possible, fall back to eager-drop. flag this in RFC.
leah: monitoring: we need per-tenant: tile_migrations, tile_failures, peak_vram_ratio, coalescer_runs, reservation_denials. also trace events for CAS failures.
samir: rollout plan: feature-flag gated, start in-host tiled copy only (no host->host). collect metrics for 48h, then enable staged host->host on canary tenants.
ben: tests: unit test for hint API; integration: simulate KV hot-scan updating pointers while migration runs; chaos: random CAS races and writer touches.
ty: performance guardrails: abort migration if bandwidth drop below threshold or migration time > 10s per allocation. emit migration_slow metric and fall back.
leah: long-term: consider evict-directed compaction vs tile-based relocation. compaction is great when slack exists; tiles for bursty stay-hot patterns. RFC should compare both with cost models (copy bytes, extra-residency, compaction work).
ops-bot: note: perf-bot recorded a baseline for tenant A: avg slab size 1.1GB, hot_fraction 12%. baseline metrics at https://telemetry.internal/redwood/tenantA/baseline
perf-bot: suggestion: include sim harness that models allocation/free over 7 days and outputs fragmentation curves for tile vs compaction strategies.
leah: ok i'll write RFC stub: "tiled scatter-gather migration + reservations + hole-coalescer". will include API sketches, rollout, tests, metrics, and Private/KMS constraints. sync tmrw 11am.
samir: +1.
ben: +1.
ty: +1.
leah: thanks all.
